verdict.rationale: Column's own docs say it originates ACH credits and debits through its API over a direct Federal Reserve integration, and that webhook endpoints can be configured for platform events. The pack does not show same-day ACH windows, or returns, NOCs and reversals modeled as first-class objects with their own webhook events, so only part of the story is evidenced. Missing for 10: same-day ACH window support, returns/NOCs/reversals as first-class API objects, ACH-specific webhook events, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can originate ACH through the API — credits and debits, same-day windows, and the unhappy paths (returns, NOCs, reversals) modeled as first-class objects with webhooks

citations.quote: ACH allows you to push (credit) funds to and pull (debit) funds from any bank account in the US. We built and operate our own direct integration with the Federal Reserve
Originate wires, ACH and book transfers, and store money in an FBO account for your customers.
You can configure webhook endpoints via APIs or Dashboard in your platform to be notified about events from Column.
To simulate incoming ACHs, we have a `/simulate/receive-ach-credit` and a `/simulate/receive-ach-debit` endpoint.
